Rameshvara Cave (Cave 21)

Cave 21 is one of the caves ASI names in its suggested 3–4 hour priority visit, and a useful stop for understanding Brahmanical rock-cut design.

Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is one monument within the UNESCO-listed Ellora Caves. Prices, opening status and routes are dated listings to re-check, not live confirmations.

Columns, panels and excavation

The Brahmanical caves at Ellora use columned interiors and sculpted panels in ways quite different from the open courtyard of Cave 16. Comparing the two makes the ambition of the monolithic temple easier to judge.

UNESCO places the Brahmanical group, Caves 13–29, broadly in the 7th–10th centuries. A group-wide range is not a precise date for any single cave.

In a short itinerary

ASI suggests a 3–4 hour visit can prioritise Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34. If time is limited, keep Cave 16 as the main stop and add Cave 21 only if it is open and within your walking capacity.

ASI describes the scarp as nearly 2 km long, so internal distances are part of the decision.

Reviewed 9 November 2026. Confirm current access and any conservation closures with ASI.

Admission and conduct

Access follows the ASI-listed Ellora Caves admission and the sunrise-to-sunset window with a weekly Tuesday closure. Avoid touching carved surfaces, respect religious imagery and stay out of closed areas.

Frequently asked questions

Why is Cave 21 often recommended?

ASI includes it in a suggested priority selection for a 3–4 hour visit to the property.

Is it close to Cave 16?

It is in the same property, but this guide does not publish a measured walking distance. ASI describes the scarp as nearly 2 km long.

Does it need a separate ticket?

The ASI listing describes admission for the Ellora Caves property. Confirm current arrangements with ASI.
